title: Malaysian-Style Fish Head Curry with Okra and Aubergine
summary: Fish heads simmered in a tangy tamarind curry with aubergine, okra, curry leaves and green chillies, finished with a little coconut milk. Served with fluffy white rice.
equipment: large deep sauté pan or wide casserole (30 cm) with lid

ingredients.item: large fish heads (such as red snapper or salmon), split in half lengthways, gills removed, rinsed
ingredients.note: ask the fishmonger to split them; or use 500 g snapper fillet in 5 cm pieces

ingredients.item: aubergine, cut into 2 x 7 cm batons
fine sea salt or table salt
okra, stem ends trimmed, halved on the diagonal

steps.title: Mix the spice paste
steps.text: Whisk the ground coriander, cumin, fennel, paprika, cayenne, turmeric and pepper with the 100ml water until smooth. Hydrating ground spices before frying them stops them scorching in the hot pan.

steps.title: Brown the aubergine
steps.text: Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in the pan over medium-high heat and brown the aubergine for 2 minutes per side. It does not need to cook through at this stage. Searing gives it colour and a slightly smoky flavour; set it aside on the plate.

steps.title: Temper the seeds
steps.text: Turn the heat down to medium-low, add the remaining 2 tbsp oil with the mustard and fenugreek seeds, and cook for about 30 seconds until the mustard seeds pop. Keep an eye on the fenugreek, as it turns bitter if it goes dark. Blooming whole seeds in oil releases their aroma into the fat.

steps.title: Build the base
steps.text: Add the onion and cook for 6-7 minutes until soft, then the garlic and ginger for 1 minute and the tomatoes for 8-10 minutes until they break down. Stir in the spice paste and cook for 5 minutes until thick and the oil starts to separate at the edges. That separating oil is the sign the spices are properly cooked and no longer taste raw.

steps.title: Simmer the fish heads
steps.text: Add the curry leaves for 1 minute, then the tamarind, the 500ml water and the salt, scraping the base of the pan. Lay in the fish heads with the aubergine, okra and chillies, making sure the liquid reaches at least two-thirds of the way up the heads, topping up with a little water if needed. Bring to the boil, cover, reduce the heat and simmer for 15-20 minutes, spooning sauce over now and then, until the flesh at the cheeks and collar is opaque, flakes from the bone and reads at least 63°C.

steps.title: Cook the rice
steps.text: Meanwhile, rinse the rice until the water runs clear, put it in the saucepan with the 450ml water and bring to the boil. Cover, cook on the lowest heat for 15 minutes, then leave it to rest off the heat for 10 minutes. The rest lets moisture even out, so the grains are tender throughout.

steps.title: Finish with coconut
steps.text: Gently stir in the sugar and coconut milk and simmer for 5 minutes, then taste. The coconut softens the tamarind's sourness and rounds out the heat. Serve with the rice and set out a bowl for the bones.

tips: A common mistake is burning the fenugreek seeds, which makes the whole curry bitter; take them off the heat as soon as the mustard seeds pop.
Ask the fishmonger to split the heads and remove the gills, which are bitter and must not go into the pot.
If fish heads are hard to find, snapper fillet pieces work well; they cook through quickly, so check them early.
Stir gently once the fish heads are in, so the flesh stays on the bone until serving.
storage: Cool within 2 hours, refrigerate and eat within 2 days. Reheat gently in a covered pan until piping hot (74°C).
